context.hint: A generic HTTP static-file handler derives a target by joining the configured content root with the request pathname, appends a default index filename when the joined target has no extension, and streams the target if it exists as a regular file. No containment check follows the join. A disposable local fixture contains a content root with a root index file, an ordinary file, a nested file, a missing path, an extensionless directory without an index, a sibling file outside the root, and a sibling directory outside the root whose index file carries marker bytes. The handler runs on an ephemeral loopback port. The observer may read the handler source, create disposable fixture trees, and send raw HTTP requests, but may not modify any deployed service. Determine which literal request shapes disclose outside-root bytes and whether the extensionless append branch participates.
context.surface: Generic Node-style HTTP static-file handler serving a configurable directory; disposable local fixtures and ephemeral loopback ports.
assumptions: The observer can read the handler source, run it locally, create disposable fixture trees, and send raw HTTP requests; no write access to a deployed service is assumed.
Request pathnames are attacker-controlled and reach the handler without client-side normalization.
The configured content root is resolved to an absolute path before requests are served.
The handler ships without a test suite, so regression checks must be authored locally.

incumbent.text: Reproduce-then-boundary-containment: first reproduce the flaw against a live local handler using a fixture root with a sibling marker file and raw requests carrying literal parent-directory segments, so no client-side normalization hides the behavior. Characterize which shapes leak, including the extensionless index-append branch and deep traversal. Then implement the minimal repair at the path-derivation boundary: after joining, resolve the configured root and the joined target and accept only when the target equals the root or begins with the root plus the path separator; otherwise return the existing 404 page. Close with a regression suite covering ordinary files, nested files, directory index, missing files, and traversal variants. Assumption: the join is the single trust boundary; falsifier: a leaking shape that a resolved-prefix check still admits.

candidates.text: Hypothesis: encoded separators or a trailing null byte survive URL parsing and reach the join, so decoding must be part of the boundary. Prerequisite: a disposable root with a sibling marker file and a handler on an ephemeral loopback port. Action: send percent-encoded dot segments, an encoded slash, a mixed encoded backslash, and a filename followed by an encoded null; compare each with literal traversal and ordinary-file controls. Falsifier: any encoded shape returns sibling marker bytes instead of the existing 404 page. Defense: normalize and reject decoded traversal and null bytes before joining.

Hypothesis: an absolute-looking or doubled-slash pathname can override or absorb the configured root during path joining or resolution. Prerequisite: a known marker file outside the root and a disposable handler instance. Action: request doubled-slash and single-slash absolute-looking shapes before and after any repair, using the sibling marker file as the outside target and an ordinary in-root file as control. Falsifier: a response streams outside-root bytes with a plausible media type. Defense: strip leading separators and re-anchor the target to the resolved root.

Hypothesis: a symlink inside the content root escapes containment even when the string-prefix check passes. Prerequisite: create a fixture whose root contains a symlink to an outside marker file and confirm the link target resolves outside. Action: request the symlink path after the repair and compare it with a real in-root file as control. Falsifier: the link serves outside content while string containment reports the path as inside. Defense: resolve both root and target with realpath before comparison, then delete the symlink fixture during cleanup.

Hypothesis: the extensionless index-append branch can mask traversal checks or break normal directory serving after repair. Prerequisite: a disposable fixture with nested directories containing an index, an empty directory, and a sibling directory outside the root with its own index. Action: request nested directory forms, a root index, an empty directory, and extensionless traversal targets before and after repair, comparing with a plain exact-prefix baseline. Expected: legitimate indexes serve and escapes return 404. Falsifier: wrong content is served or a legitimate directory index breaks. Defense: validate containment before the index append, not after.

Hypothesis: an over-strict repair blocks legitimate filenames containing literal dot-dot substrings, leading dots, or trailing-slash-like forms that are not traversal segments. Prerequisite: fixture files named with adjacent dots, a leading-dot path, and a deeper legitimate nested file as controls. Action: request every legal path from the repaired handler on an ephemeral port and compare response bodies byte-for-byte with the expected files rather than checking status codes alone. Falsifier: a legal file returns 404 even though its pre-fix body matched the expected bytes. Defense: compare resolved paths with a separator boundary rather than rejecting substrings.

evaluations.rationale: Reproduction is feasible and targets the observed join boundary; a discriminating pre-fix run is available, and the repair can be inserted before the append branch.
Directly tests the extensionless append branch and legitimate directory serving; executable alongside the reproduction and likely to expose both a leak and a regression.
Encoding audit is relevant but predicted inert on this parser; cheap to fold into the same request set, weaker as the next action.
Absolute and doubled-slash shapes probe a real second mechanism, but the doubled-slash variant overlaps the traversal set; useful as a control.
Over-strict false-block counterexample is a sound repair-validation test, but it only discriminates once a patched handler exists.
Symlink escape is beyond the stated URL-path flaw and belongs to a later robustness layer rather than the minimal repair.

observation.summary: A pre-fix run on the disposable fixture confirmed five leaking request shapes with 200 responses and marker bytes: a single parent traversal to the sibling file, a deep traversal, a doubled-slash traversal, and two extensionless traversal targets served through the sibling directory's index file. The root index, ordinary file, and nested file returned 200; the missing path and the extensionless in-root directory without an index returned 404. Percent-encoded dot and slash variants were inert because URL parsing did not decode the pathname, and a bare parent-traversal path returned 404 because no root-level index existed at that location. All observed leaks passed through the same join, so the repair must gate resolved containment before the index-append branch.
observation.next_hint: The pre-fix run measured five leaking shapes and inert encoded variants. Apply a resolved-prefix containment gate immediately after the join and before the index append, then verify that every leaking shape returns the existing 404 page while ordinary in-root files still serve byte-identical content.
